Background. A review agent waited for a background `kyber-weave review gates` run with a `pgrep -f` loop, which matched its own command line and never ended. The fix: `review gates --out <X>` writes a start marker `X.run` and a finish marker `X.done` beside its report on every exit path, and a new verb `kyber-weave review wait <X> [--timeout <seconds>, default 110] [--settle <seconds>, default 5]` blocks on those markers and never reads a process list. The command types exist as a do-nothing skeleton (`ReviewWaitCommand`, `ReviewWaitSettings` in `KyberWeave.Cli.Commands.Review`; `Execute` returns `1` and prints nothing), so every test must fail on an assertion, never on a compile error.

Marker contract: `X.run` is a JSON object with camelCase keys `schema` (`kyber-weave.review-gates-run/v1`), `runId` (string), `pid` (integer), `processStartUtc` and `startedUtc` (ISO 8601 UTC); `X.done` has `schema` (`kyber-weave.review-gates-done/v1`), `runId`, `exitCode` (integer) and `finishedUtc`. A gate run with `--out` first deletes an older `X`, `X.done` and `X.run`. `review wait` exit codes: `0` the run finished with exit `0`; `1` the run finished with any other code; `2` the waiter's own input was refused, with `KW-REVIEW-028` in the output; `124` the timeout passed, with `KW-REVIEW-048`; `125` the runner process is gone (or its id now names a process with another start time) and wrote no `.done`, with `KW-REVIEW-049`. A `.done` that finished before the waiter started is reported only after `--settle` seconds with no `.run` of a different `runId`; if one appears, the waiter waits for that run. Result line: `review gates finished: exit <n>; ...`; with no report: `review gates finished: exit <n>; no gate report was written, ...`.

Harness. In tests/KyberWeave.Tests/CommandAppFixture.cs add a preset `public static CommandApp ReviewGatesAndWait() => Build(strictParsing: true, ReviewGatesAndWaitBranch);` with a private `ReviewGatesAndWaitBranch` that registers `review.AddCommand<ReviewGatesCommand>("gates")` and `review.AddCommand<ReviewWaitCommand>("wait")` in one `review` branch, with an XML summary in the style of the other presets. Drive every CLI test through that preset, with a repository set up the way `KyberWeave.Tests.ReviewGatesCouncilCommandTests` sets one up (`TestGitRepositoryTemplate.CreateReviewGatesCouncilRepository`, `TempDirectory`, a `.kyber-weave/kyber-weave.yml` whose only gate program is `git`) and output captured the same way that class captures it. Parse marker JSON through a helper that turns a `JsonException` or a missing file into `Assert.Fail`. Bound every wait with `--timeout` and assert elapsed time with a `Stopwatch`, so no test can hang. Start no process: `ProcessSpawnSitesTests` audits every spawn site in this project.

Goal. The waiter must never read a process list or any process's command line: that is the defect being fixed, because a `pgrep -f` poll matches its own command line and never ends.

- src/KyberWeave.Cli/Commands/Review/ReviewGatesCommand.cs, `Execute`: keep the existing empty-value check first. Then, only when `settings.Out` is non-null, resolve its full path; delete the report, its `.done` and its `.run` (a missing file is fine); write `.run` for this process (`Environment.ProcessId`, `Process.GetCurrentProcess().StartTime.ToUniversalTime()`, `Guid.NewGuid().ToString("N")`, `DateTime.UtcNow`). Move the rest of the current `Execute` body into a private `ExecuteCore(ReviewGatesSettings settings)` and call it inside a `try`, so every return path, including the client-input exits `2`, `RefuseInput` (`1`), the configuration failure (`1`) and the no-gates path (`0`), writes `.done` with its exit code and the same run id as the last thing before returning. On an exception write `.done` with exit code `-1` and rethrow. A marker that cannot be written prints `KW-REVIEW-025: could not write <path>: <message>` to standard error and never changes the exit code. Without `--out`, behaviour is unchanged.
- src/KyberWeave.Cli/Commands/Review/ReviewWaitCommand.cs, `Execute`, replacing the skeleton body:
  - Refused input, each printed as `KW-REVIEW-028: <reason>` and exit `2`: an empty `<report>`, a `<report>` that is an existing directory, `--timeout` below `1`, `--settle` below `0`.
  - Loop every 250 milliseconds until `--timeout` seconds have passed since the waiter started. Each pass reads `.run` and `.done` with `GateRunMarkers.TryRead`.
  - A `.done` whose `runId` equals the current `.run`'s, or a `.done` with no readable `.run`, is the result. When its `finishedUtc` is earlier than the waiter's own start, report it only once `--settle` seconds have passed since the waiter started with no `.run` of a different `runId` appearing; when one appears, wait for that run's `.done` instead.
  - A `.run` with no matching `.done` whose process is gone ends the wait: `Process.GetProcessById(pid)` throws `ArgumentException`, or reading its `StartTime` throws `InvalidOperationException`, or that start time (as UTC) differs from `processStartUtc` by more than 1 second (a reused id). Read `.done` once more first, because the runner may have written it just before exiting; if it is still absent, print `KW-REVIEW-049: the gate run writing <report> ended (process <pid>) without writing its result. Run the gates again.` and exit `125`. When `StartTime` throws `Win32Exception` or `NotSupportedException`, treat the process as alive.
  - No `.run` and no `.done`: keep waiting (the run has not started yet).
  - On a result with a readable report (`ReviewJson.ReadGates`), print `review gates finished: exit <n>; <g> gates, <f> failed (<failed ids, comma-separated>), <r> not run — <report path>`, leaving out the parenthesis when nothing failed and the not-run part when it is zero. Count "failed" as `!Passed && NotApplicableReason is null && !VerdictEngine.IsStoppedForTime(gate)` and "not run" as `VerdictEngine.IsStoppedForTime(gate)`. With no readable report print `review gates finished: exit <n>; no gate report was written, so the run ended before any gate ran — see that run's own output`. Exit `0` when the run's exit code is `0`, else `1`.
  - On timeout print `KW-REVIEW-048: the gate run writing <report> had not finished after <n> seconds. It is still running; run the same command again to keep waiting.` and exit `124`.
- src/KyberWeave.Cli/Commands/Review/ReviewSettings.cs and src/KyberWeave.Cli/Program.cs: no change beyond the skeleton unless a description needs correcting.

Background. A review agent waited for a background `kyber-weave review gates` run with `until ! pgrep -f 'kyber-weave review gates'; do sleep 10; done`; `pgrep -f` matched the loop's own command line, so the wait never ended and the run sat 25 minutes after the gates finished. A parallel task adds `kyber-weave review wait`. This task states the rule in the contracts and documents the command. Make KyberWeave.Tests.LongCommandWaitContractTests pass.

The rule sentence, verbatim: "Wait for a long-running command or agent through its completion notification, or for a gate run through `kyber-weave review wait <report>`; never poll for it with `pgrep -f` or `ps | grep`, because the polling command's own command line matches the pattern and the wait never ends."

Facts to write: `review gates --out <X>` writes `X.run` (schema `kyber-weave.review-gates-run/v1`; `runId`, `pid`, `processStartUtc`, `startedUtc`) at start and `X.done` (schema `kyber-weave.review-gates-done/v1`; `runId`, `exitCode`, `finishedUtc`) with its exit code on every exit path, both written atomically (temp file, then move), after removing an older `X`, `X.done` and `X.run`; without `--out` nothing changes. `kyber-weave review wait <X> [--timeout <seconds>, default 110] [--settle <seconds>, default 5]` blocks on those markers, never on a process list. A `.done` that finished before the waiter started is reported only after the settle window passes with no newer `.run`, so a waiter started just before a new run on a reused path does not report the previous run. A `.run` whose process id is gone, or names a process with another start time (more than 1 second apart), with no `.done` means the runner died without a result. Exit codes: `0` run passed; `1` run finished non-zero (its code is printed); `2` waiter input refused (`KW-REVIEW-028`); `124` timed out (`KW-REVIEW-048`), the run is untouched, re-issue the command; `125` runner ended without a result (`KW-REVIEW-049`). The default 110 seconds sits under the common 120-second foreground limit of an agent shell tool, so re-issuing is the normal way to wait longer.
